p: in which there are seven species:
and we circle once each day,
and on Hoshana Rabbah seven times,
And when a person is under siege and in distress,
he cries out "Hoshi'ah na — save, please,"
the difference between help and salvation.
And we sit in the sukkah,
the four directions, above and below, and its air space.
And we shake toward all the directions
for "our will is to do Your will,
and the subjugation to the kingdoms" (Berachos 17a);
and this is "to hold back harmful winds
that it corresponds to the desires in the heart
and the thoughts in the mind;
and this is to thrust away the leaven in the dough,
we circle with the Sefer Torah,
to bring the words of Torah into the heart permanently.
For from Hashem's side we find
(מִדְרַשׁ חָזִית, שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, ד):
the words of Torah were implanted in their hearts,
and they would learn and not forget;
and afterward, at the time they heard
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts," etc. —
for these two include the 248 positive commandments
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאָדָם כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים לד, טו)
But from the side of man it is written (Tehillim 34:15),
one must first remove the bad
the words of Torah can enter the heart.
Therefore, after they have circled the seven days
to thrust away all the bad,
אַחַר כָּךְ יוּכְלוּ לְהַקִּיף בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה,
afterward they can circle with the Sefer Torah,
which we circle in order to bring permanently
the words of Torah into the heart.
Likewise, beforehand we circled with the lulav
for a person to refine himself
And afterward we circle with the Sefer Torah
to bring in the holiness of the seven Ushpizin
only through prayer and from Hashem's side;
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, ב)
as is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 104b)
that on this day the Ushpizin come themselves.
